distractors.reason: 'Careful' is an adjective. Adverbs of manner are needed after the verb 'listen'.
'Care' is a noun, so it cannot describe how someone listens. We say 'take care', not 'listen care'.
This adverb means without attention. It is the opposite of what the poem needs and is not the natural partner of 'listen'.

example_sentence: Please listen ___ to every line of the poem.
l1_interference: Os falantes de português às vezes colocam o advérbio antes do verbo, dizendo 'carefully listen' em vez de 'listen carefully', porque em português o advérbio pode vir antes do verbo.
explanation: In English, the adverb usually comes after the verb it describes. 'Listen carefully' is the natural word order, and 'carefully' is the usual partner of 'listen'.

related_collocations.example: She can speak English fluently after two years of study.
Our teacher asked us to read the poem aloud.
He recited the poem beautifully at the school event.

memory_tip: The adverb usually comes AFTER the verb: listen carefully, speak fluently, read aloud
